cards.subtitle: Something Just Happened

abilities.name: Surge
abilities.text: Trades a week of volume inside four minutes for reasons unpublished.

abilities.name: Attention
abilities.text: Every screen in the market turns toward the same ticker at once.

abilities.name: Reveal Later
abilities.text: Explains itself forty minutes afterward, when the move is complete.

cards.weakness: It never says which direction is right.
cards.lore: Volume is the only honest signal on the chart, because it cannot be drawn afterward. A spike means something happened, and says nothing about what. By the time the reason is published, the participants who knew have already finished.

traits.label: Evidence
traits.text: Proof that something real occurred.

traits.label: Silence
traits.text: Reports magnitude without reporting cause.

traits.label: Precedence
traits.text: Arrives before the announcement it reflects.

traits.label: Brevity
traits.text: The signal is over before it is understood.

cards.flavor: Volume never lies, and never explains.

cards.name: The Dust
cards.subtitle: Too Small to Move

abilities.name: Settle
abilities.text: Remains in the wallet as a remainder worth less than moving it.

abilities.name: Unspendable
abilities.text: The fee to send it exceeds everything it has ever been worth.

abilities.name: Dusting Attack
abilities.text: Arrives unrequested, from a stranger, to link addresses that preferred separation.

cards.weakness: It is worth less than its own fee.
cards.lore: Dust is what remains after every swap: fractions too small to spend and too stubborn to vanish. Most of it is harmless clutter. Some of it was sent deliberately, to see which wallets belong to the same person.

traits.label: Remainder
traits.text: The fraction left after every imperfect trade.

traits.label: Inertia
traits.text: Cannot be moved for less than it is worth.

traits.label: Clutter
traits.text: Accumulates in every wallet that gets used.

traits.label: Surveillance
traits.text: Unwanted dust can be a tracking device.

cards.flavor: Worth less than the fee to move it.

cards.name: The Gas Fee
cards.subtitle: Pay the Road, Not the Driver

abilities.name: Meter
abilities.text: Charges for computation by the step, honestly, whether or not it succeeds.

abilities.name: Spam Shield
abilities.text: Makes infinite nonsense expensive, which is the entire security model.

abilities.name: Fee Spike
abilities.text: Prices ordinary users out of their own chain for an afternoon.

cards.weakness: It cannot tell urgent from trivial.
cards.lore: The fee is not a tax but a price, and the price is the only thing standing between an open network and infinite garbage. It is fair, transparent, and occasionally absurd. Everyone complains about it and nobody has a better idea.

traits.label: Metering
traits.text: Every step of computation has a posted price.

traits.label: Defence
traits.text: Spam is prevented by making it expensive.

traits.label: Volatility
traits.text: Costs pennies at dawn and fortunes at noon.

traits.label: Fairness
traits.text: The same rules apply to every wallet.

cards.flavor: Blockspace is scarce. Complaining is free.

cards.name: The Pending Transaction
cards.subtitle: Neither Sent Nor Kept

abilities.name: Broadcast
abilities.text: Leaves the wallet and enters a queue with no promised end.

abilities.name: Stuck
abilities.text: Underpriced by one unit and forgotten by every block producer.

abilities.name: Replace By Fee
abilities.text: Pays more to overwrite an earlier self that refused to arrive.

cards.weakness: Only a higher fee ends the waiting.
cards.lore: Between signed and settled lies a stretch of time that feels much longer than it is. The funds are gone from the wallet and absent from the destination. Refreshing the explorer does not help, and everyone does it anyway.

traits.label: Suspension
traits.text: Gone from one place, not yet in another.

traits.label: Underpayment
traits.text: One unit too cheap and the queue forgets it.

traits.label: Compulsion
traits.text: Refreshed forty times without effect.

traits.label: Remedy
traits.text: Escaped only by paying more.

cards.flavor: Signed, sent, and nowhere at all.

cards.name: The Confirmation
cards.subtitle: Now It Is Real

abilities.name: Include
abilities.text: Places the transaction into a block and into history simultaneously.

abilities.name: Deepening
abilities.text: Each block afterward makes reversal more expensive than any attacker can afford.

abilities.name: Settled
abilities.text: Ends every dispute permanently, including the ones with a good argument.

cards.weakness: Finality protects mistakes too.
cards.lore: Confirmation is the moment the intention becomes a fact, without a clearing house or a business day. Six blocks later, undoing it costs more than the world can justify. The relief it produces is the closest thing this world has to a handshake.

traits.label: Finality
traits.text: Settlement without a bank or a Tuesday.

traits.label: Depth
traits.text: Each block makes reversal less affordable.

traits.label: Relief
traits.text: The waiting ends and the fact begins.

traits.label: Indifference
traits.text: Confirms errors with equal enthusiasm.

cards.flavor: Six blocks deep and no appeals court.

cards.name: The Block Reward
cards.subtitle: Wages of the Chain

abilities.name: Pay Out
abilities.text: Rewards whoever did the work, without an employer or a contract.

abilities.name: Security Budget
abilities.text: Buys defence from strangers who have never spoken to each other.

abilities.name: Diminishing
abilities.text: Shrinks on schedule until fees must carry the entire burden alone.

cards.weakness: It does not last forever.
cards.lore: The reward is how a network without a payroll hires its own defenders. It arrives on time, in public, to whoever earned it, and nobody signs anything. Its slow disappearance is the great unfinished question of the design.

traits.label: Wages
traits.text: Paid by protocol rather than by employer.

traits.label: Openness
traits.text: Anyone may compete for it; nobody may deny it.

traits.label: Schedule
traits.text: Shrinks predictably and without negotiation.

traits.label: Question
traits.text: What secures the chain when the wage ends.

cards.flavor: A payroll with no employer at all.

cards.name: The Nonce
cards.subtitle: Used Once, Then Never

abilities.name: Increment
abilities.text: Counts each transaction so no message can ever be replayed.

abilities.name: Strict Order
abilities.text: Nothing after a gap will execute until the gap is filled.

abilities.name: Guess Forever
abilities.text: Answers the mining puzzle only by being tried a quadrillion times.

cards.weakness: One skipped number halts everything after.
cards.lore: The nonce is the least glamorous number in this world and one of the load-bearing ones. It makes replay impossible and ordering absolute, using nothing but counting. In mining it is the lottery ticket, discarded by the trillion until one wins.

traits.label: Counting
traits.text: Security from a number that only goes up.

traits.label: Ordering
traits.text: Transactions execute in sequence or not at all.

traits.label: Disposability
traits.text: Trillions are tried and thrown away every second.

traits.label: Obscurity
traits.text: Nobody thinks about it until it blocks them.

cards.flavor: One number, used once, never again.

cards.name: The Hash
cards.subtitle: One Way, No Return

abilities.name: Digest
abilities.text: Turns anything of any size into the same short unreadable string.

abilities.name: Avalanche
abilities.text: One changed character produces an output sharing nothing with the last.

abilities.name: Prove Without Showing
abilities.text: Demonstrates possession of a document while revealing none of it.

cards.weakness: It proves sameness, never meaning.
cards.lore: The hash is the quiet primitive under everything else here: blocks, addresses, signatures, proofs. It is a one-way door that always returns the same answer and never explains it. Trust in this world is mostly trust that this function keeps its promise.

traits.label: Determinism
traits.text: The same input always yields the same output.

traits.label: Avalanche
traits.text: A single character rewrites the entire result.

traits.label: One Way
traits.text: Easy forward, impossible backward.

traits.label: Foundation
traits.text: Every other guarantee here rests on it.

cards.flavor: Easy one way, impossible the other.

cards.name: The Private Key
cards.subtitle: The Only Sovereignty

abilities.name: Sign
abilities.text: Proves ownership to the entire world without revealing itself once.

abilities.name: Sole Authority
abilities.text: No court, company, or committee can override what it decides.

abilities.name: Lose It
abilities.text: Ends the claim permanently, with the balance still visible to everyone.

cards.weakness: Nobody can reissue it.
cards.lore: A private key is a number large enough that guessing it is not a strategy. Whoever holds it is the owner, in the only sense this world recognises. There is no appeal, no reset link, and no institution standing behind the loss.

traits.label: Ownership
traits.text: Possession and title are the same thing.

traits.label: Proof
traits.text: Signs without ever being disclosed.

traits.label: Finality
traits.text: No authority exists above it.

traits.label: Burden
traits.text: Total control arrives with total responsibility.

cards.flavor: A number nobody can guess or reissue.

cards.name: The Public Address
cards.subtitle: A Name Without a Face

abilities.name: Receive
abilities.text: Accepts value from anyone, anywhere, without approval or introduction.

abilities.name: Public Ledger
abilities.text: Every payment ever received remains visible to every curious stranger.

abilities.name: Deanonymised
abilities.text: One careless withdrawal links a lifetime of activity to a legal name.

cards.weakness: Pseudonymous is not anonymous.
cards.lore: The address is an identity with no paperwork, issued by mathematics rather than an institution. It accepts payment from anyone and reveals its history to everyone. Privacy here is a practice, not a property, and most people discover that late.

traits.label: Openness
traits.text: Anyone may pay it without asking permission.

traits.label: Exposure
traits.text: Its whole history is public by design.

traits.label: Neutrality
traits.text: Does not care who is sending or why.

traits.label: Linkage
traits.text: One connection to a name exposes everything.

cards.flavor: Pseudonymous until one careless connection.

cards.name: The Paper Wallet
cards.subtitle: Ink Against Time

abilities.name: Print
abilities.text: Moves a fortune onto a sheet that no network can reach.

abilities.name: Offline
abilities.text: Immune to every remote attack and every remote backup.

abilities.name: Fade
abilities.text: Surrenders to damp, sunlight, or a tidy relative with a recycling bin.

cards.weakness: Paper burns, fades, and gets tidied away.
cards.lore: For a few years the safest place for a fortune was a printer and a drawer. The method is genuinely secure against the internet and helpless against ordinary life. More of these were lost to house moves than to hackers.

traits.label: Airgap
traits.text: Utterly unreachable by any remote attacker.

traits.label: Simplicity
traits.text: Requires no battery, firmware, or update.

traits.label: Decay
traits.text: Ink fades and thermal paper surrenders entirely.

traits.label: Domestic Risk
traits.text: Lost to spring cleaning more often than to crime.

cards.flavor: Safe from hackers, helpless against housekeeping.

cards.name: The Exchange Floor
cards.subtitle: Where Everyone Meets

abilities.name: Match
abilities.text: Pairs a buyer and a seller who will never learn each other's names.

abilities.name: Always Open
abilities.text: No closing bell, no holidays, and no hour without a price.

abilities.name: Halt Withdrawals
abilities.text: Closes the doors during the exact hour everyone chose to leave.

cards.weakness: The doors are controlled from inside.
cards.lore: The Floor never closes, which means the panic never has to wait until morning. It is the most useful place in this world and the least aligned with it. Every generation learns the same lesson about whose balance sheet the balance sits on.

traits.label: Depth
traits.text: Where price is discovered for everyone else.

traits.label: Sleeplessness
traits.text: Open through every holiday and every crisis.

traits.label: Custody
traits.text: Convenience purchased with somebody else's keys.

traits.label: Doors
traits.text: Opened and closed at the operator's discretion.

cards.flavor: No closing bell means no cooling off.

cards.name: The Waiting Room
cards.subtitle: Queued, Indefinitely

abilities.name: Hold Position
abilities.text: Places a request in a queue and shows a number that never moves.

abilities.name: Under Review
abilities.text: Every enquiry receives the same message from a different name.

abilities.name: Approved Later
abilities.text: Releases the request one week after it stopped mattering at all.

cards.weakness: Nothing here can be appealed or hurried.
cards.lore: Between a request and a resolution sits a room with no clock. Verification, review, and maintenance are all names for the same wait. The ledger settles in minutes; the humans around it take considerably longer.

traits.label: Opacity
traits.text: No position, no estimate, no explanation.

traits.label: Delay
traits.text: Resolves eventually, on nobody's schedule.

traits.label: Anxiety
traits.text: The waiting costs more than the outcome.

traits.label: Contrast
traits.text: Settlement is fast; permission is slow.

cards.flavor: The chain settled. The ticket did not.

cards.name: The Trading Desk
cards.subtitle: Six Screens, One Chair

abilities.name: Watch
abilities.text: Monitors four venues, three chains, and one increasingly hostile chair.

abilities.name: No Close
abilities.text: A market that never sleeps produces a trader who barely does.

abilities.name: Walk Away
abilities.text: Closes every screen for a weekend and returns measurably better at this.

cards.weakness: The market outlasts any human schedule.
cards.lore: The desk is where discipline is either practised or discovered to be absent. More screens do not produce more edge, but they do produce more hours. The traders who survive are the ones who learned when to leave the chair.

traits.label: Vigil
traits.text: Built for a market with no closing bell.

traits.label: Overload
traits.text: More screens rarely mean more clarity.

traits.label: Ritual
traits.text: The routine matters more than the setup.

traits.label: Rest
traits.text: The strongest position is often no position.

cards.flavor: The market never sleeps. Someone must.

cards.name: The Basement Rig
cards.subtitle: Warmth in Winter

abilities.name: Build It
abilities.text: Assembles a machine from parts, patience, and one extremely brave power strip.

abilities.name: Space Heater
abilities.text: Warms an entire floor of the house as a side effect.

abilities.name: Early Days
abilities.text: Earns coins that mean nothing now and everything a decade later.

cards.weakness: Industry arrived and never left.
cards.lore: Before the warehouses there were bedrooms, garages, and one long extension cord. The rigs were loud, hot, and assembled by people who mostly wanted to see whether it worked. Everything industrial about this world began as a hobby with a fan problem.

traits.label: Tinkering
traits.text: Built by hand from parts and curiosity.

traits.label: Heat
traits.text: Heats the house whether or not that was wanted.

traits.label: Amateurism
traits.text: Ran for the joy before it ran for margin.

traits.label: Obsolescence
traits.text: Outcompeted by warehouses within a single cycle.

cards.flavor: It began as a hobby with fans.

cards.name: The Server Farm
cards.subtitle: Cathedral of Noise

abilities.name: Rack Up
abilities.text: Turns a warehouse and a power contract into a share of the network.

abilities.name: Economy Of Scale
abilities.text: Buys electricity at a price no household will ever be offered.

abilities.name: Curtail
abilities.text: Sells its power back to the grid and earns more than mining would.

cards.weakness: It cannot move when the price does.
cards.lore: What began in basements now occupies buildings with their own substations. Efficiency won, as it always does, and the romance moved out. The machines are quieter about it than the people who miss the old arrangement.

traits.label: Industry
traits.text: Hobby replaced by procurement and logistics.

traits.label: Power
traits.text: Negotiates electricity like a smelter, because it is one.

traits.label: Immobility
traits.text: Cannot relocate when conditions change.

traits.label: Efficiency
traits.text: Wins on margin, and only on margin.

cards.flavor: Romance lost to procurement and cheap power.

cards.name: The Whitelist
cards.subtitle: The Chosen Few

abilities.name: Grant Access
abilities.text: Admits a chosen list before the doors open to anyone else.

abilities.name: Manufactured Scarcity
abilities.text: Turns a queue into a status symbol and a status symbol into demand.

abilities.name: Insider Slots
abilities.text: Reserves the best allocation for wallets that never completed a single task.

cards.weakness: Access is not the same as value.
cards.lore: The whitelist converts attention into obligation: perform enthusiasm now, receive permission later. Most of the work asked for is theatre, and everyone involved knows it. The genuinely favoured names were on the list before the tasks were invented.

traits.label: Gatekeeping
traits.text: Permission granted before the public is invited.

traits.label: Theatre
traits.text: Tasks performed sincerely for a spot on a spreadsheet.

traits.label: Status
traits.text: Being chosen matters more than what is received.

traits.label: Favouritism
traits.text: The best slots were allocated privately.

cards.flavor: Permission dressed as a reward for loyalty.

cards.name: The Blacklist
cards.subtitle: Frozen Where It Stands

abilities.name: Freeze
abilities.text: Renders a balance visible, permanent, and completely unusable.

abilities.name: Guilt By Contact
abilities.text: Wallets that merely touched a flagged address inherit the suspicion.

abilities.name: Blocked Forever
abilities.text: Marks an address in a registry with no removal process at all.

cards.weakness: It only works where issuers can reach.
cards.lore: Censorship resistance ends where a centralised issuer begins. A frozen balance is still on the ledger, still visible, and no longer anyone's. It is a reminder that not every token in this world obeys the same rules.

traits.label: Freeze
traits.text: The balance remains and the ownership does not.

traits.label: Contagion
traits.text: Proximity to a flagged address is treated as intent.

traits.label: Asymmetry
traits.text: Applies to issued tokens, not to the base asset.

traits.label: Silence
traits.text: No process exists for arguing back.

cards.flavor: Still on the ledger, owned by nobody.

cards.name: The Referral Link
cards.subtitle: Friendship, Commissioned

abilities.name: Share
abilities.text: Recommends a venue warmly and earns a percentage of every subsequent trade.

abilities.name: Compounding
abilities.text: Pays forever on the activity of everyone recruited, and their recruits.

abilities.name: Recruit Everyone
abilities.text: Converts an entire social circle into a revenue line.

cards.weakness: Trust spends only once.
cards.lore: The referral link turns friendship into distribution and pays for the conversion. The recommendation may even be sincere; the incentive is present regardless. Its greatest cost is that nobody can be certain which was which afterward.

traits.label: Commission
traits.text: Every recommendation carries a hidden fee.

traits.label: Compounding
traits.text: Earns from recruits and their recruits forever.

traits.label: Ambiguity
traits.text: Sincere advice and paid advice look identical.

traits.label: Cost
traits.text: Spends a relationship to earn a percentage.

cards.flavor: Advice is cheaper when it pays commission.

cards.name: The Roadmap
cards.subtitle: Quarter Four, Every Year

abilities.name: Announce Phase
abilities.text: Promises a milestone in a quarter that is comfortably distant.

abilities.name: Vague Timeline
abilities.text: Uses seasons rather than dates, so lateness is never technically possible.

abilities.name: Silent Revision
abilities.text: Republishes the plan with the missed items quietly absent.

cards.weakness: Dates make promises measurable.
cards.lore: A roadmap is a hypothesis presented with the confidence of a schedule. The honest ones ship two of five items and say which three slipped. The rest discover that a plan without dates can never be broken.

traits.label: Ambition
traits.text: Describes a future more clearly than the present.

traits.label: Vagueness
traits.text: Seasons instead of dates, on purpose.

traits.label: Revision
traits.text: Edited quietly rather than explained loudly.

traits.label: Signal
traits.text: Shipping anything at all outperforms most of the field.

cards.flavor: Seasons, not dates. Never technically late.

cards.name: The Alpha Call
cards.subtitle: Whispered to Nine Hundred

abilities.name: Drop Ticker
abilities.text: Shares a name with a private group that is not remotely private.

abilities.name: Tiered Exit
abilities.text: The earliest tier sells into the tier that heard it second.

abilities.name: Paid Group
abilities.text: Charges a monthly fee for information already priced in by dawn.

cards.weakness: Shared information is not an edge.
cards.lore: The call arrives urgently, exclusively, and simultaneously to several thousand people. Each tier of the audience is the exit for the tier above it. By the time it reaches the paying members, the only thing left to buy is the story.

traits.label: Urgency
traits.text: Demands action before verification is possible.

traits.label: Tiering
traits.text: Every layer is liquidity for the one before.

traits.label: Decay
traits.text: Worthless within an hour of being shared.

traits.label: Exclusivity
traits.text: Private, in the sense of nine hundred members.

cards.flavor: Exclusive to a few thousand close friends.

cards.name: The FUD
cards.subtitle: Doubt, Weaponised

abilities.name: Seed Doubt
abilities.text: Asks a question that cannot be answered and never claimed anything.

abilities.name: Faster Than Truth
abilities.text: Travels three days ahead of any correction and is never overtaken.

abilities.name: Sometimes Right
abilities.text: Occasionally describes the fraud accurately and is ignored for months.

cards.weakness: Some of it is simply true.
cards.lore: Doubt is cheap to manufacture and expensive to disprove, which makes it an excellent weapon and an occasional public service. The same rumour that destroys an honest project also warns about a dishonest one. Nobody can tell which is which until afterward.

traits.label: Velocity
traits.text: Outruns every correction ever issued.

traits.label: Deniability
traits.text: Only asked a question, technically.

traits.label: Weaponised
traits.text: Cheap to produce and costly to answer.

traits.label: Accuracy
traits.text: Sometimes the warning was correct.

cards.flavor: Doubt costs nothing and travels free.

cards.name: The FOMO
cards.subtitle: Everyone Else Is Winning

abilities.name: Chase
abilities.text: Buys the fourth green candle at four times the size originally planned.

abilities.name: Timeline Pressure
abilities.text: Every screenshot is proof that waiting has already cost something.

abilities.name: Top Tick
abilities.text: Executes the largest order of the year within nine minutes of the high.

cards.weakness: There is always another opportunity.
cards.lore: Fear of missing out is the most reliable liquidity in this market. It converts a plan into a purchase and a purchase into a lesson. The feeling is real, urgent, and almost never correct about the timing.

traits.label: Urgency
traits.text: Converts a plan into an immediate order.

traits.label: Comparison
traits.text: Measures success against everybody else's best day.

traits.label: Size Creep
traits.text: The position grows with the fear, not the thesis.

traits.label: Recurrence
traits.text: There is always another one arriving.

cards.flavor: The feeling is real. The timing rarely.

cards.name: The Capitulation
cards.subtitle: The Last Seller

abilities.name: Give Up
abilities.text: Sells everything at once, for relief rather than for price.

abilities.name: Exhaustion
abilities.text: Removes the final seller and, with them, the reason to keep falling.

abilities.name: The Bottom
abilities.text: Marks the low that nobody recognises until eleven months afterward.

cards.weakness: It is only obvious in hindsight.
cards.lore: Capitulation is not a price but a decision made by everyone at roughly the same time. The selling is not strategic; it is the end of caring. Which is precisely why the bottom is built there, unwitnessed and unannounced.

traits.label: Surrender
traits.text: Sold for peace rather than for value.

traits.label: Volume
traits.text: The heaviest day, and the least considered.

traits.label: Exhaustion
traits.text: Nothing falls further once nobody is left.

traits.label: Invisibility
traits.text: Recognised only much later, by accident.

cards.flavor: The bottom is built by people leaving.

cards.name: The Accumulation
cards.subtitle: Boring on Purpose

abilities.name: Buy Quietly
abilities.text: Adds a little every week while nobody is discussing the asset.

abilities.name: Sideways
abilities.text: Produces months of flat charts that drive away every impatient holder.

abilities.name: Base Built
abilities.text: Creates the floor that the next season stands on without credit.

cards.weakness: It requires believing during silence.
cards.lore: Accumulation is the least photogenic phase and the only profitable one to be early in. Nothing happens for months, which is the mechanism rather than a failure of it. Everything the next cycle celebrates was purchased here, quietly, by people who were bored.

traits.label: Boredom
traits.text: Nothing happens, deliberately, for a long time.

traits.label: Discretion
traits.text: Bought without announcement or applause.

traits.label: Duration
traits.text: Measured in quarters rather than sessions.

traits.label: Foundation
traits.text: Every later rally stands on this floor.

cards.flavor: Nothing happens, and that is the point.

cards.name: The Reset
cards.subtitle: Begin Again, Wiser

abilities.name: Close Everything
abilities.text: Exits every position and sits in cash without a thesis.

abilities.name: Clean Slate
abilities.text: No bags, no leverage, and nothing left to defend publicly.

abilities.name: Begin Again
abilities.text: Returns with smaller size, written rules, and considerably better results.

cards.weakness: Starting over costs the years already spent.
cards.lore: Every survivor here has reset at least once, usually after being certain they would not need to. The account goes to zero or to cash, and the lessons are the only inventory carried forward. The second attempt is quieter and works better.

traits.label: Humility
traits.text: Admits the plan was the problem.

traits.label: Flatness
traits.text: No position is also a position.

traits.label: Rules
traits.text: Returns with something written down.

traits.label: Cost
traits.text: Wisdom purchased at full retail price.

cards.flavor: Everyone here has started over once.

cards.name: The Architect — Ghost of Genesis
cards.subtitle: Built It, Then Left

abilities.name: Write It
abilities.text: Publishes a working system to an audience that mostly ignores it.

abilities.name: Never Spend
abilities.text: Holds an untouched fortune that has not moved in over a decade.

abilities.name: Disappear
abilities.text: Hands over the keys, sends a last message, and is never seen again.

cards.weakness: A myth cannot correct the record.
cards.lore: The Architect built the thing, handed it to strangers, and walked out before the money arrived. The fortune sits at known addresses and has never moved, which is the only proof of intent anyone will ever get. Every founder since has been measured against a silence they cannot match.

traits.label: Restraint
traits.text: Left the greatest fortune here untouched, deliberately.

traits.label: Anonymity
traits.text: No face, no interviews, no follow-up project.

traits.label: Handover
traits.text: Gave the keys away while the work still mattered.

traits.label: Absence
traits.text: The most influential figure here is not present.

cards.flavor: Built it, gave it away, said nothing since.
